legend: Polycarp is very fond of playing the game Minesweeper. Recently he found a similar game and there are such rules.

There are mines on the field, for each the coordinates of its location are known (xi,yi%%ZSMJ0%%). Each mine has a lifetime in seconds, after which it will explode. After the explosion, the mine also detonates all mines vertically and horizontally at a distance of k%%ZSMJ1%% (two perpendicular lines). As a result, we get an explosion on the field in the form of a "plus" symbol ('+'). Thus, one explosion can cause new explosions, and so on.

Also, Polycarp can detonate anyone mine every second, starting from zero seconds. After that, a chain reaction of explosions also takes place. Mines explode instantly and also instantly detonate other mines according to the rules described above.
Polycarp wants to set a new record and asks you to help him calculate in what minimum number of seconds all mines can be detonated.
input: The first line of the input contains an integer t%%ZSMJ2%% (1≤t≤104%%ZSMJ3%%) — the number of test cases in the test.
An empty line is written in front of each test suite.
Next comes a line that contains integers n%%ZSMJ4%% and k%%ZSMJ5%% (1≤n≤2⋅105%%ZSMJ6%%, 0≤k≤109%%ZSMJ7%%) — the number of mines and the distance that hit by mines during the explosion, respectively.

Then n%%ZSMJ8%% lines follow, the i%%ZSMJ9%%-th of which describes the x%%ZSMJ10%% and y%%ZSMJ11%% coordinates of the i%%ZSMJ12%%-th mine and the time until its explosion (−109≤x,y≤109%%ZSMJ13%%, 0≤timer≤109%%ZSMJ14%%). It is guaranteed that all mines have different coordinates.
It is guaranteed that the sum of the values n%%ZSMJ15%% over all test cases in the test does not exceed 2⋅105%%ZSMJ16%%.
output: Print t%%ZSMJ17%% lines, each of the lines must contain the answer to the corresponding set of input data  — the minimum number of seconds it takes to explode all the mines.
note: 0%%ZSMJ18%% second: we explode a mine at the cell (2,2)%%ZSMJ19%%, it does not detonate any other mine since k=0%%ZSMJ20%%.
1%%ZSMJ21%% second: we explode the mine at the cell (0,1)%%ZSMJ22%%, and the mine at the cell (0,0)%%ZSMJ23%% explodes itself.
2%%ZSMJ24%% second: we explode the mine at the cell (1,1)%%ZSMJ25%%, and the mine at the cell (1,0)%%ZSMJ26%% explodes itself.
0%%ZSMJ27%% second: we explode a mine at the cell (2,2)%%ZSMJ28%% we get:

1%%ZSMJ29%% second: the mine at coordinate (0,0)%%ZSMJ30%% explodes and since k=2%%ZSMJ31%% the explosion detonates mines at the cells (0,1)%%ZSMJ32%% and (1,0)%%ZSMJ33%%, and their explosions detonate the mine at the cell (1,1)%%ZSMJ34%% and there are no mines left on the field.
